title: At the Doctor's / Dɔgɔtɔrɔ yɛ
bridge: Sipanilɛn, kalankalanw bɛ ka kɛ fana la, an bɛ se ka ‘me duele’ kɔfɛ a bɛ se ka ‘me duele la cabeza’. Anglisenw, sintaksɛyɛ min bɛ yaya: ‘I have’ + ‘a headache’ (ayɛ ayi sanjɛ). An ka tɔɔrɔw bɛrɛ minw bɛ yaya ‘I hurt my head’ ma sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la. Kɔfɛ, anglisenw, ‘hurt’ bɛ se ka dumaw, ‘My head hurts’ (ayi sanjɛ ayɛ). ‘Have’ dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ kɛ sanjɛ dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ lajɛ ‘hurt’ dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ kɛ kalankalanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ bɛrɛbɛrɛ lajɛ fɔlɔw ka tɔgɔ cogo di an ka sɔrɔla ka sɔrɔ angayɛni ye.
rule: A2 tɔgɔ la, kalankalanw kelen kelen koo la, an bɛ se kɔfɛ: 1) ‘I have’ + dumandɛ (a headache, a cold, a fever, a cough, a sore throat, a stomachache, lanw) ma sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ka kɛyɔrɔn. 2) ‘My [kalankalan fɔlɔ] hurts’ wala ‘My [kalankalan fɔlɔ] is sore’ ma kalankalan fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ. 3) ‘I feel’ + jɛnɛw bɛɛ (sick, dizzy, tired, lanw) ma sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ kelen kelen. Fɔlɔw ka kɛyɔrɔn koo la, an bɛ se ka ‘do/does’ (Do you have...? Yes, I do. No, I don’t). Fɔlɔw ka kɛyɔrɔn koo la, an bɛ se ka ‘should’ / ‘shouldn’t’ (You should rest, You shouldn’t eat spicy food). ‘Hurt’ dumaw min bɛ yaya ‘hurt - hurt - hurt’ ye. ‘Me duele’ bɛ se ka kɔfɛ fana; kalankalanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ bɛrɛbɛrɛ lajɛ ‘My head hurts’ (ala ‘I hurt my head’ sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la). ‘I’ve got’ bɛ yaya ‘I have got’ ka jɛnɛw kan (I’ve got a cold). Kɔfɛ fɔlɔw ka kɛyɔrɔn koo la, an bɛ se ka ‘I have a cold’.

concept_examples.translation: Ayɛ ayi sanjɛ ayɛ ayi gɛlɛn sanjɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˈhɛdeɪk ənd ə sɔːr θroʊt/

concept_examples.text: Do you have a fever?

concept_examples.text: You should drink a lot of water.

common_error.explanation: Jɛnɛ min bɛ yaya ‘me duele la cabeza’ ka jɛnɛ kan ‘I hurt my head’ ye. ‘Hurt’ dumaw min bɛ yaya dumaw ka dumaw la, a ka tɔɔrɔw bɛ yaya kalankalanw ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ (ayi gɛlɛn sanjɛ ayɛ). Sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la, ‘have a headache’ wala ‘my head hurts’ bɛ se ka kɔfɛ. ‘Hurt’ dumaw min bɛ yaya dumaw ka dumaw la (ala dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ) ma sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ka kɛyɔrɔn, nka, kalankalanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ bɛrɛbɛrɛ lajɛ (my head hurts). ‘Have’ + dumandɛ bɛ se ka sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ lajɛ.

examples.original: I have a cold.
examples.translation: Ayɛ sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ayɛ.
examples.note: ‘Have’ + sanjɛ wala sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ bɛ se ka kɔfɛ. ‘I am cold’ ala se ka sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la, a se ka ayɛ sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ye.

examples.original: I have a cough and a runny nose.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə kɒf ænd ə ˈrʌni noʊz/
examples.translation: Ayɛ kufaw ayɛ ayɛ gɛlɛn ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ.
examples.note: Sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ka kɛyɔrɔn ‘and’ bɛ se ka kɔfɛ: cough and runny nose. ‘Runny nose’ (gɛlɛn ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ) fɔlɔ la.

examples.original: I feel dizzy.
examples.translation: Ayɛ sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ayɛ.
examples.note: ‘Feel’ + jɛnɛw bɛ se ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ kelen kelen. ‘I feel me’ ala se ka kɔfɛ fana.

examples.original: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Ayɛ na wuli kaanu hɛrɛ fɔlɔ fɔlɔ.
examples.note: ‘Take’ dumaw bɛ se ka wuli kaanu la, ala ‘drink’ (na). ‘Twice a day’ se ka hɛrɛ fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la.

examples.original: You should rest in bed.
examples.translation: Ayɛ tɛ ayɛ na fɔlɔ fɔlɔ.
examples.note: Fɔlɔw ka kɛyɔrɔn koo la, ‘should’ + dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ bɛ se ka kɔfɛ. A se ka ‘must’ (tɔɔrɔw) fana.

examples.original: I need to make an appointment.
examples.translation: Ayɛ tɛ ayɛ na kɛyɔrɔn kan.
examples.note: ‘Make an appointment’ bɛ se ka kɛyɔrɔn kan ka kɛyɔrɔn la. ‘Need to’ + dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ se ka tɔɔrɔw ye.

examples.original: My back hurts a lot.
examples.translation: Ayɛ gɛlɛn sanjɛ ayɛ bɛɛ.
examples.note: ‘A lot’ bɛ se ka dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ cogo wala dumandɛyɛyɛbɔ ka jɛnɛ kan la. ‘My back hurts much’ ala se ka kɔfɛ fana ‘a’ ala b’a se ka kɔfɛ fana.

examples.original: I have a sharp pain in my chest.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ʃɑːrp peɪn ɪn maɪ tʃɛst/
examples.translation: Ayɛ sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ayɛ gɛlɛn.
examples.note: ‘Sharp’ bɛ se ka sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la, ‘dull’ bɛ se ka sanjɛ kanw fɔlɔ fɔlɔ la. ‘In my + kalankalan fɔlɔ’ bɛ se ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ka kɛyɔrɔn la.

examples.original: My knee is swollen and red.
examples.translation: Ayɛ gɛlɛn ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ayɛ bɛɛ ayɛ jɛnɛw.
examples.note: ‘Is’ + jɛnɛw bɛ se ka sanjɛyɛrɛyɛbɔ ka kɛyɔrɔn la. ‘Swollen’ jɛnɛw min bɛ yaya jɛnɛw kan ye.

title: Booking Accommodation / Ka jamana kɛra
bridge: Espagnol kan, mɔgɔ min b'a ka sɔrɔ 'reservo una habitación' tiɲɛ kan. Alaŋ kan, 'would like' + 'to book' b'a fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ka kɛ. A bɛɛ, a ban tɛ ka sira bɛɛ kan: espagnol kan 'habitación doble' ka fɔ, alaŋ kan 'double room' ka fɔ. A bɛɛ, alaŋ kan 'for' b'a sɔrɔ jamana kɛra ka saba ta a ka jɔ ka taara fɔ (for two nights), espagnol kan 'por dos noches' ka fɔ.
rule: A2 tɔgɔ kɔrɔsi alaŋ kan ka jamana kɛra fɔ, bɔ a ma ka kɛ: 'I would like to book...' (Mɛn ka taa ka jamana kɛ...), 'I'd like to make a reservation' (Mɛn ka taa ka jamana kɛra fɔ). A ban tɛ ka sira bɛɛ kan, o ma ka kɛ: 'My name is...'. Jɔn ka tɛmɛ tɔɔrɔ kan, o ma ka kɛ 'on' jɔn kan (on Monday) e 'for' jamana kɛra ka saba ta a ka jɔ ka taara fɔ (for three nights). A ma ka bɔ o sɔrɔ jamana kɛra ka taa kelen, o ma ka kɛ: 'Do you have...?' (A bɛ jamana kɛra ka taa kelen bɛ?) to 'Is there...?' (A bɛ jamana kɛra ka taa kelen bɛ?). Jamana kɛra ka tɔɔrɔ bɛɛ: 'single room' (jamana kɛra ka taa kelen), 'double room' (jamana kɛra ka taa fali), 'twin room' (jamana kɛra ka taa fali). Alaŋ kan, tɛmɛ tɔɔrɔ bɛɛ ka sira bɛɛ kan, tɛmɛnyumaa + tɛmɛ.

common_error.correct_alt: I'd like to book a room for two nights.
common_error.explanation: Espagnol kan, mɔgɔ min b'a ka sɔrɔ 'quiero reservar' tiɲɛ kan 'querer' ka jamana kɛra fɔ. Alaŋ kan, 'want' b'a fɔlɔ fɔlɔ ka kɛ e ka taa saba. 'Would like' (ka taa ka taa) b'a yɛrɛ fɔlɔ. A bɛɛ, alaŋ kan 'would like' ka hɛrɛ 'to' + tɛmɛnyumaa b'a sɔrɔ: 'I would like to reserve'. O sɔrɔ tɛ 'I want reserve' (alaŋ kan 'to' ka taa). A bɛɛ, 'book' (ka jamana kɛra) b'a sɔrɔ fɔlɔ fɔlɔ.

examples.original: How much is it per night?
examples.translation: A ka taa ka jamana kɛra ka taa kelen bɛra?

examples.original: Does the price include breakfast?
examples.translation: A ka taa ka jamana kɛra ka tɔɔrɔ bɛɛ bɛ a ka taa ka tɛmɛn tɔgɔ?
examples.note: Tɛmɛnyumaa ka tɔɔrɔ bɛɛ, o ma ka kɛ 'Does'. 'Include' ka tɔɔrɔ, tɛmɛnyumaa ka sira bɛɛ.

examples.original: Is Wi-Fi free?
examples.translation: Wi-Fi bɛɛ bɛ a ka taa ka jamana kɛra ka taa kelen?

examples.original: What time is check-out?

examples.note: 'Check-out' ka tɔɔrɔ, jamana kɛra ka taa ka fɔ. 'Check-in' ka tɔɔrɔ, jamana kɛra ka taa ka jɔ.

title: At the Bank or Exchange Office / Baani kanu ye kɔfɛ kanu
bridge: A taali giin na, k'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne 'I would like...' anw fɔne 'Can I...?', nka, a taali giin na, o k'o fɔ ne 'Quisiera...' anw fɔne '¿Me da...?'. O ye fana, a taali giin na, k'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne 'can' anw fɔne 'would' ka bɔ verb mabɔkɛ, 'to' tun mabɔkɛ, nka, a taali giin na, o k'o fɔ ne 'some' anw fɔne 'any' ka bɔ a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ. A taali giin fana, k'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne '100 dollars' ka bɔ 'one hundred dollars', nka, a taali giin na, o k'o fɔ ne 'fifty dollars' ka bɔ 'cincuenta dólares'.
rule: K'a baara baani kanu ye kɔfɛ kanu ra, o k'o fɔ ne 'I would like' (me gustaría) ka bɔ a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ. A fɔkɔ fana, o k'o fɔ ne 'Can I...?' (¿Puedo...?) k'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn. K'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne 'What is the exchange rate?' (¿Cuál es el tipo de cambio?). Faga fɔne, a taali giin na, k'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne 'some' (afirmativo) anw fɔne 'any' (negativo/pregunta). A fɔkɔ fana, o k'o fɔ ne a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ ka bɔ a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ. K'a fɔ a bɔ a kun dɔn, o k'o fɔ ne a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ ka bɔ a fɔko fana, a fɔko kanu, anw a fɔko kɛlɛ.

title: Job Interview Basics / Faranw kɛyɔgɔ cɛnko ka jamana
bridge: Faranw kɛyɔgɔ cɛnko kanw ka jamana jɛnɲɔgɔnya la, banki bɛɛ min bɛ na fɔlɔ fɔlɔnin ka kɛ. A fɔrɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ solɔbali/kɛmɛbali 'tú' ka jamana; 'you' bɛɛ min bɛ ka tɛ. A go, bɛ ka tɛmɛ prɛzɛnsi simpli mɔgɔw ka sɛbɛn fɔ koɲuman, ni pasɛ simpli mɔgɔw ka sɛbɛn fɔ faranw kɛyɔgɔ kanw la.
rule: Mɔgɔw ka sɛbɛn fɔ koɲuman la, tɛmɛ 'I am' (ne den) ni 'I have' (ne jamana). Mɔgɔw ka sɛbɛn fɔ mɔgɔw ka jamana la, tɛmɛ prɛzɛnsi simpli: 'I work as...' (ne bɛna...). Mɔgɔw ka sɛbɛn fɔ faranw kɛyɔgɔ kanw la, tɛmɛ pasɛ simpli: 'I worked at...' (ne bɛna...). Banki bɛɛ min bɛ na fɔlɔ fɔlɔnin ka kɛ: 'What do you do?' (I ka jamana nɛ?), 'Why do you want this job?' (I fɛ i ja mɔgɔ wɛrɛ fɛ?), 'What are your strengths?' (I ka saba ka tɔgɔ bɛɛ?). Faga nɔɔrɔla, a fɔrɔ min bɛ ka tɛmɛ sujɛ ka kɛ.

title: At the post office / Bɔri jɛkuru la
bridge: Aŋkaloŋkan, bɔri jɛkuru la kɛ fɔlɔwulɛ ni ɛnrɛwulɛw la, i ka jamana kanbɔlɔ filimuw bɛɛ min bɛ fɔlɔ ‘I need to’ ni ‘I’d like to’ ka jamana kanbɔlɔ filimuw. Hivɛlaŋ, a ka ‘send’ ka jamana kanbɔlɔ filimuw bɛɛ min bɛ fɔlɔ ‘to’ ka jamana kanbɔlɔ filimuw (send something to someone), nka, a ye ko ‘enviar algo a alguien’. Talaki fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘How much does it cost?’, nka, a ye ko ‘¿Cuánto cuesta?’.
rule: A2 tɛmɛna, bɔri jɛkuru la kɛ fɔlɔwulɛ ni ɛnrɛwulɛw la, fɔlɔwulɛw yaayɔrɔ filimuw: 1) ‘I need to + verbo’ (necesito + infinitivo) fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘I need to send this package.’ 2) ‘I’d like to + verbo’ (me gustaría + infinitivo) fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘I’d like to buy some stamps.’ 3) ‘How much is/are...?’ ni ‘How much does it cost?’ fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘How much is the shipping?’ 4) ‘to’ fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘send’ ni ‘mail’ ka jamana kanbɔlɔ filimuw, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘Send it to my friend.’ 5) ‘where’ ni ‘when’ fɔlɔwulɛw la, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ‘Where can I pick up my package?’ Talenki, aŋkaloŋkan, ɛnrɛwulɛw la fɔlɔ ɛnrɛyɛlɪ (registered mail), nka, a ye ko ‘correo certificado’.

title: Renting a Flat / Ka flati ka kɛra
bridge: Españiyakulan, kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra, an ka flati kɛ kɛra ka sira kan, an ka sɛbɛn'izɛyɛrɛyɛrɛ kan. Angalekɛyirakɔnɔ, an ka kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra, an ka flati kɛ kɛra ka sira kan, an ka sɛbɛn'izɛyɛrɛyɛrɛ kan. Taga bɛɛ, an ka kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra, an ka flati kɛ kɛra ka sira kan, an ka sɛbɛn'izɛyɛrɛyɛrɛ kan.
rule: A2 tɔgɔ kɛyɔrɔw la, kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra, an ka flati kɛ kɛra ka sira kan, an ka sɛbɛn'izɛyɛrɛyɛrɛ kan: (1) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra: 'to rent' (kɛra). (2) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra: 'for rent' (kɛra don). (3) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra: 'available' (kɛra ka sira). (4) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra: 'apartment' (flati), 'flat' (flati, Angalɛkani kɛyɔrɔw la), 'landlord' (kɛra don kɔfɛ), 'tenant' (kɛra ka sira), 'deposit' (kɛra don kɔfɛ), 'rent' (kɛra don kɔfɛ), 'lease' (kɛra don kɔfɛ). (5) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra: 'How much is the rent?' (Kɛra don kɔfɛ tɛ mɔgɔ min bɛ yɛ?) 'Is it furnished?' (A bɛ yɛ fɛɛnɛyɔrɔ?) Kɛra don kɔfɛ ka kan kɛra, an ka flati kɛ kɛra ka sira kan, an ka sɛbɛn'izɛyɛrɛyɛrɛ kan.

title: Making small talk at a party / Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ
bridge: Espaɲɛ kan, kalansa lajɛ fɛ kan mɛn dɔw, an bena sɔrɔ ‘¿Qué tal?’ wala ‘¿Cómo estás?’ an ka ‘estar’ jamana bɛɛminɛ na kɛ fana. A fɛn, an bena ‘How are you?’ amma an ka ‘How's it going?’ wala ‘What's up?’ bɛɛ ka di an ka sɔrɔkɛlɔ fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ. Kɛlɛsanw fɛ, a fɛn, ‘estoy de acuerdo’ sira ‘I am agree’ (kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ) bɛɛ an ka sɔrɔkɛlɔ, amma ‘I agree’ bɛɛ. Kɔfɛ, ‘How are you?’ sira bɛɛ an ka jɔnkɔfɛlɔw bɛɛ min bɛɛ, ‘I'm good, thanks’, an ka sɔrɔkɛlɔ fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, Espaɲɛ kan mɛn dɔw, an ka sɔrɔkɛlɔw bɛɛ min bɛɛ.
rule: Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɔɔrɔ fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ sɔrɔkɛlɔw bɛn ‘Hey, how's it going?’ wala ‘What's up?’ (jɔnkɔfɛlɔ: ‘Not much, you?’). Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɔɔrɔ ‘I'm [name], nice to meet you’. Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɔɔrɔ ‘Would you like something to drink?’ (fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ sɔrɔkɛlɔ) wala ‘Do you want a drink?’ (fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ sɔrɔkɛlɔ). Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɔɔrɔ ‘I like...’ / ‘I don't like...’. Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɛɛminɛ ‘agree’ (fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ sɔrɔkɛlɔ ‘be agree’): ‘I agree with you’. ‘How are you?’ sira bɛɛ an ka jɔnkɔfɛlɔw bɛɛ min bɛɛ: ‘I'm good’, ‘I'm fine’, ‘Pretty good’. Kɛlɛsanw fɛɛw kanu lajɛ fɛ, bɔɔrɔ ‘It was nice talking to you’ wala ‘See you later’.

title: Complaining and Apologizing / Kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi
bridge: Espaɲɛ kan, o kɛlɛsanw bɛ laawandi la, o b'a kan 'lo siento' wala 'perdón' bɛɛ fana. Nka, angale kan, 'I'm sorry' a fana ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, a 'excuse me' bɛɛ a kan kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la wala kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la. Kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, angale kan b'a kan 'can't' wala 'won't' bɛɛ fana ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, nka espaɲɛ kan o b'a kan 'no puedo' wala 'no quiere' bɛɛ fana ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la. Talaki fɔlɔ wɛrɛ bɛɛ laawandi la, o taa kan 'to' bɛɛ fana ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, a 'sorry' bɛɛ fana ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la.
rule: Kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, o taa kan 'I can't + verbo' (manti ayi ka taa) wala 'This is + adjetivo' (o yɛrɛ + adjetivo). Laawandi la, o taa kan 'I'm sorry (for) + gerundio' wala 'I apologize for + sustantivo'. Talaki fɔlɔ wɛrɛ bɛɛ laawandi la, 'sorry' bɛɛ a kan 'for' ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la (I'm sorry for being late). Kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, 'I apologize' bɛɛ a kan ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la. Kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la, o taa kan 'It's okay', 'No problem', wala 'That's fine'. Manti o taa kan 'I'm sorry' ka kɛlɛya kɛlɛsanw bɛɛ laawandi la (o taa kan 'excuse me').

title: Describing your hometown / N'a taama wɛrɛ fɛ
bridge: Dɔnkɔrɔkanbɔri la, n'a taama wɛrɛ fɛ fana, i ka sɔrɔla 'to be' bɔ i ka fɔ a ka taa-taa (big, small, quiet) ane 'there is/there are' bɔ i ka sɔrɔla tɛmɛ fɔlɔw. Hispanikanbɔri fɔ a ka se ka di 'es grande' wala 'hay un parque', nka, dɔnkɔrɔkanbɔri la, fɔ o fɔmɔɲɔgɔ 'there is' a b'a fɔ singular ane 'there are' a b'a fɔ plural. O yɔrɔ, dan fɔlɔw ka taa-taa ka tɔgɔ: taa-taa kelen ye sɔrɔla kelen, fɔlɔw fana 'My city is big'. Hispanikanbɔri ka jamana bɔ mɔgɔw ye fɔ a ka se ka di 'there is/are' wala i ka dan fɔlɔw ka taa-taa ka tɔgɔ sɔrɔla cogo di, fɔlɔw fana 'the city big' koo fana 'the big city'.
rule:
A2 tɔgɔ la, n'a taama wɛrɛ fɛ dɔnkɔrɔkanbɔri la, bɔ sunfɛyagaw ye:

1. **Taa-taa + sɔrɔla 'to be' (am/is/are) + taa-taa fɛ**: Taa-taa kelenye fɛew ka taa-taa. Fɔlɔw fana: 'My town is small.' (Mi pueblo es pequeño).
   - Pronɔn fɔlɔw la: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we are, they are.
   - Taa-taa fɛew ka taa-taa ka tɔgɔ sɔrɔla cogo di: 'a big city', koo fana 'a city big'.

2. **There is / There are**: A b'a fɔ a ka se ka di tɛmɛ kanu ye n'a taama ra.
   - There is + tɛmɛ singular/contable fɔlɔw: 'There is a park.' (Hay un parque).
   - There are + tɛmɛ plural: 'There are two schools.' (Hay dos escuelas).
   - Negatif la: There isn't / There aren't: 'There isn't a cinema.' (No hay cine).
   - Fɔgɔ: Is there...? Are there...? (¿Hay...?).

3. **Tɛmɛw ka tɛmɛyaŋgaw**: Tɛmɛw ka tɛmɛyaŋgaw fɔgɔ.
   - 'in the center' (en el centro), 'on the corner' (en la esquina), 'near' (cerca de), 'next to' (al lado de).

4. **Sɔrɔla ka jamana**: 'You can see', 'you can find', 'there is' a b'a fɔ a ka se ka di 'se puede encontrar'.

5. **Sɔrɔla fɛew ka taa-taa**: Bɔ 'and' fɔ i ka taa-taa fɛew ka tɔgɔ ane 'but' bɔ i ka taa-taa fɛew ka tɔgɔ: 'My town is small but beautiful.' (Mi pueblo es pequeño pero bonito).

A2 la, sɔrɔla fɛew ka taa-taa ka tɔgɔ koo sɔrɔla fɛew ka taa-taa ka tɔgɔ. Fɔ o fɔmɔɲɔgɔ 'there is' ka plural 'there are' ye – o fɔ a ka se ka di 'there is many shops'.

title: Talking About Hobbies / Faran ka jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu
bridge: Espagnol la, faran ka jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu ma, mɛn na verb ‘gustar’ an ka ‘encantar’ an ka ‘me gusta’, ‘te gusta’ tɛmɛ kanu. Faran kɔrɔsi, verb ‘like’ ka tɔgɔ: ‘I like + -ing’ an ka ‘I like + to + verb’. Faran kɔrɔsi, mɛn b’a taa ka taa jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu ‘on Mondays’ (los lunes), amma espagnol la, mɛn na ‘los lunes’ ka taa. Faran kɔrɔsi, mɛn na ‘do’ ka jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu ‘What do you do in your free time?’, amma espagnol la, mɛn na ‘¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?’ ka taa.
rule: Faran ka jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu (A2 tɔgɔ): verb ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ an ka ‘prefer’ tɛmɛ kanu, an ka noun an ka verb -ing tɔgɔ (tɛmɛntɔ, ‘I like music’, ‘I love playing soccer’). Mɛn na ‘be interested in’ + noun an ka -ing tɔgɔ (tɛmɛntɔ, ‘I’m interested in photography’). Faran ka kɛlɛ, mɛn na ‘What do you like doing?’ an ka ‘What do you do in your free time?’. Faran ka taa jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu, mɛn na adverb tɛmɛ ‘always’, ‘usually’, ‘sometimes’, ‘never’ ka verb tɔgɔ (tɛmɛntɔ, ‘I usually read’). Mɛn na preposition ‘in’ (in my free time), ‘on’ (on weekends, on Mondays) an ka ‘at’ (at home, at the weekend – faran kan british). Jɔn ka bɔ: mɛn b’a taa ‘do’ ‘like’ tɛmɛ kanu present simple la (mɛn na ‘I like’, ‘I do like’ tɛmɛ kanu, a bɛɛ kanu fɔlɔw ka taa).

concept_examples.text: I like listening to music.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛn na musiqi kan.

concept_examples.text: She loves playing tennis.
concept_examples.translation: A ka tɛni sii ka taa.

concept_examples.text: What do you do in your free time?
concept_examples.translation: I kɛlɛ i jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt duː juː duː ɪn jɔː friː taɪm/

concept_examples.text: I usually go hiking on weekends.
concept_examples.translation: Sɔsɔmɔgɔ la, mɛn na jamana bɛɛw kanu.

common_error.explanation: Kɛlɛw bɛɛ ka taa, mɛn na ‘me gusta jugar’ ka taa infinitive tɛmɛ kanu, amma an ka mɔgɔw tɛmɛ faran ka tɔgɔ. Amma, faran la, ‘like’, ‘love’, ‘enjoy’ tɔgɔw bɛɛ ka bɛɛ, mɛn na -ing tɔgɔ an ka ‘to’ tɛmɛ infinitive tɔgɔ (amma mɛn b’a taa infinitive ‘to’ tɛmɛ kanu). A ka fɔlɔw kanu, fɔlɔw ‘like’ tɛmɛ, mɛn na -ing tɔgɔ: ‘I like playing’. Mɛn na ‘I like to play’ tɛmɛ, amma a bɛɛ kanu fɔlɔw ka taa.

levels.label: Talking About What You Like
levels.translation: Faran ka i jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu

examples.original: I love reading books.
examples.translation: Mɛn na tɛmɛsi tɔgɔ.
examples.note: ‘Love’ + -ing tɛmɛ kanu i jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘encantar’ ka taa.

examples.original: She enjoys painting.
examples.translation: A ka tɛmɛ sii ka taa.
examples.note: ‘Enjoy’ tɛmɛ kanu -ing tɔgɔ. Mɛn b’a taa ‘enjoy to paint’.

examples.original: I don't like cooking.
examples.translation: Mɛn b’a tɛmɛ sii ka taa.
examples.note: Faran ka taa, mɛn na ‘don’t’ + like + -ing. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘no me gusta’.

examples.original: What do you like doing?
examples.translation: I kɛlɛ i tɛmɛ ka taa?
examples.note: A ka taa jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu kɛlɛw ka taa. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘¿Qué te gusta hacer?’.

examples.original: Do you play any sports?
examples.translation: I ka tɛni sii ka taa?
examples.note: ‘Play’ tɛmɛ kanu team sport tɔgɔ (play football, play tennis). Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘jugar’.

examples.original: How often do you go to the cinema?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ ˈɒfən duː juː ɡəʊ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə/
examples.translation: I sɔrɔ cinɛ ka taa bɛɛ?
examples.note: Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘ir al cine’ ‘a’ tɛmɛ kanu; faran la, mɛn na ‘go to + lugar’.

levels.label: Expressing Frequency and Preferences
levels.translation: Taa jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu an ka i tɔgɔ

examples.original: I often watch TV in the evening.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɒfən wɒtʃ ˌtiːˈviː ɪn ðə ˈiːvnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Sɔsɔmɔgɔ la, mɛn na televiziɔn kan kɛlɛya.
examples.note: Adverb tɛmɛ (often, usually, always) tɛmɛ kanu verb tɔgɔ. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘a menudo’.

examples.original: I prefer playing video games to reading.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ prɪˈfɜː ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈvɪdiəʊ ɡeɪmz tə ˈriːdɪŋ/
examples.translation: Mɛn na videɔ jeu tɔgɔ ka tɛmɛsi tɔgɔ.
examples.note: Faran ka tɔgɔ tɛmɛ, mɛn na ‘prefer A to B’, A an ka B -ing tɔgɔ. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘prefiero X a Y’.

examples.original: On Sundays, I usually go for a walk.
examples.phonetic: /ɒn ˈsʌndeɪz aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli ɡəʊ fər ə wɔːk/
examples.translation: Kari jamana la, sɔsɔmɔgɔ la, mɛn na bɛɛw kanu.
examples.note: ‘On’ tɛmɛ kanu jamana dɔgɔtɔrɔw kanu. Espagnol la, mɛn na ‘los domingos’.
